Zod objects strip unknown keys by default, so when credential sync is enabled the parsed response drops the expiry field. In GoogleCalendarService, `token.expiry_date` would then be undefined, and the updated credential would always look expired, forcing a refresh on every use. adjudication.rationale: In `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, when sync mode is enabled it uses `minimumTokenResponseSchema = z.object({ access_token: z.string(), [z.string().toString()]: z.number(), ... })`. Zod objects are `strip` by default, so any fields not explicitly in the object shape are removed from `data`. Since real expiry fields like `expiry_date` / `expires_in` are not explicitly declared (the computed `[z.string().toString()]` keys do not act as an index signature / catchall), the parsed result will drop those expiry fields even if present. Downstream code then persists the parsed result (or relies on it), causing missing expiry info and likely triggering refresh logic repeatedly.
